abertura: In the lesson you are going to hear two people disagree for two minutes without either of them stopping.
Three of the sentences below are true. Mark those three.

itens.t: Going quiet while you think ends your turn.
itens.porque: Silence is read as “I have finished”, and the other person starts talking. Three seconds of silence costs you the turn.

itens.t: If you do not understand something, it is better to answer anyway.
itens.porque: Answering something else is how conversations go wrong quietly. Asking takes two seconds and fixes it.

itens.t: Asking the other person a question keeps the conversation going.
itens.porque: It hands the turn back, and it buys you the whole time they take to answer.

itens.t: You should only speak when you are sure your English is correct.
itens.porque: Nobody would say anything, ever. The two people you are about to hear make mistakes and neither of them stops.

itens.t: Saying something like *let me think* keeps your turn while you decide.
itens.porque: It says “I am still talking” without saying anything else. It is the cheapest three seconds in English.

itens.t: Disagreeing with someone usually ends the conversation.
itens.porque: It usually starts one. The two people in this lesson disagree the whole way through and neither of them leaves.

sec1.rationale: Three of these are about time: buying it, using it, and not losing it. That is what the lesson is about.
sec1.pt: Na aula você vai ouvir duas pessoas discordando por dois minutos, sem que nenhuma delas pare a conversa. Antes disso, marque as três frases verdadeiras sobre o que mantém uma conversa de pé.

nota.texto: Você começa conversas sozinha — isso já acontece. O que ainda não acontece é a conversa continuar depois da sua segunda frase. Hoje o assunto é o que se diz nos três segundos em que você está pensando.

sec2.titulo: Six words for what you think of something

it makes you a little sad

itens.t: disappointing
confusing

alts: I am telling the truth about a fact
I am going to say what I really think

sec2.pt: Seis palavras para dizer o que você achou de alguma coisa. Escolha o sentido que cabe. A última, honestly, você vai ouvir na aula: ela avisa que o que vem em seguida é o que a pessoa acha de verdade.

nota.texto: Ninguém diz honestly porque estava mentindo antes. É um aviso: o que vem agora é o que eu acho mesmo, e talvez não seja o que você quer ouvir. Você vai ouvir isso nos primeiros dez segundos da conversa.

sec3.titulo: Ends it, or keeps it going?
abertura: Someone has just told you what they think about a movie. Here are six possible replies.
Which ones leave the other person something to say?

itens.t: Yeah.
itens.porque: One word, no opinion, no question. The other person now has to start again from nothing.

itens.t: Really? Why do you say that?
itens.porque: It hands the turn back and asks for the one thing that is worth hearing: the reason.

itens.t: I do not know.
itens.porque: It is honest and it is a dead end. I am not sure — what do you think? is the same idea with a door left open.

itens.t: I see what you mean, but I think it is slow.
itens.porque: Disagreeing keeps a conversation alive as long as you give the reason. The part before but is what makes it safe.

itens.t: OK.
itens.porque: Sounds polite and closes everything. It is the most common way of ending a conversation you did not want to end.

itens.t: Honestly? I did not like it. What about you?
itens.porque: Opinion, and then the question back. Two moves in eight words — this is what you will be doing at the end of the lesson.

sec3.pt: Alguém acabou de dizer o que acha de um filme. Para cada resposta possível, decida: ela deixa alguma coisa para a outra pessoa dizer, ou fecha a conversa?

doc.texto:
Sam: ok I finished it
Alex: AND???
Sam: honestly, I am not sure. the first season was better
Alex: in what way though
Sam: nothing happens for four episodes. and then everything happens in twenty minutes
Alex: fair. but the last scene tho

abertura: Three of these are true. Mark those three.

itens.t: Alex asks Sam to explain.
itens.porque: in what way though. It is not a full sentence and it does the same job as “why do you say that?”

itens.t: Sam thinks the second season is better.
itens.porque: The opposite: the first season was better. The whole message is a careful way of saying no.

itens.t: Sam gives a reason with two parts.
itens.porque: Nothing happens for four episodes, and then everything happens at once. Two problems, and the second one only makes sense after the first.

itens.t: Alex agrees with Sam about everything.
itens.porque: fair. but the last scene tho — Alex concedes the point and immediately keeps their own. That is one sentence doing two things.

itens.t: Alex finds something good in it.
itens.porque: The last scene. Alex never says it is good in so many words, and you can tell anyway.

itens.t: The conversation ends because they disagree.
itens.porque: It is still going. They disagreed six messages ago and neither of them has left.

sec4.rationale: Nobody here writes a full sentence, and the conversation still has an opinion, a reason, a question and a concession in it. That is the shape you are learning to say out loud.
sec4.pt: Leia a conversa de chat entre duas pessoas e marque as três frases verdadeiras. Repare que ninguém escreve frase inteira — e mesmo assim há opinião, motivo, pergunta e concordância parcial ali dentro.

abertura: Choose the ending that belongs there. These are the moves you can use in your lesson.

itens.ok: but I still think it is slow

itens.t: That is a good question. I

sec5.pt: Cada frase começa de um jeito. Escolha o final que combina. São as cinco formulações que você pode usar em voz alta na sua aula — duas para pedir o motivo, duas para ganhar tempo, uma para discordar sem fechar.

nota.texto: Why do you say that? e What made you think that? pedem o motivo. Let me think e That is a good question compram três segundos. As duas coisas mantêm a conversa de pé, e nenhuma delas exige que você já saiba o que dizer.

abertura: Think of a real subject you have an opinion about. You can use them in your lesson.

itens.t: Honestly? I {think|80px} it is worth it.
Let me {think|80px} for a second.
Really? Why do you {say|70px} that?
I see what you {mean|80px}, but I still think I am right.

sec6.pt: Complete as quatro frases. Pense num assunto de verdade sobre o qual você tem opinião — você pode usar essas frases na sua aula, falando.

nota.titulo: Quatro frases que servem para qualquer assunto
nota.texto: Nenhuma delas tem a ver com filme. Elas funcionam sobre escola, música, uma decisão em casa, qualquer coisa — e é por isso que valem mais do que vocabulário novo.

itens.t: Tell me you liked it.
itens.porque: Maya opens by telling him what to say. She is not asking — she already knows she is going to have to fight for it.

itens.t: Honestly? No. Not really.
itens.porque: Chris's answer, and the shortest turn in the conversation. Honestly warns her before the no arrives.

itens.t: Really? Why do you say that?
itens.porque: The line the lesson is named after. She does not argue — she asks for the reason first.

itens.t: It is two hours long, and you know the ending after ten minutes.
itens.porque: The reason, and it comes only because she asked. Without her question this whole line does not exist.

itens.t: The photography is beautiful. I will give you that.
itens.porque: Chris gives her something. It comes after she pushes back, and it is what stops the conversation from becoming a fight.

itens.t: Why do you love it so much?
itens.porque: Now he asks her. The question goes both ways in this conversation, and that is why it lasts two minutes.

ord20.rationale: Look at the shape: tell — refuse — ask why — reason — concede — ask back. Only two of those six are about the movie.

itens.t: Tell me you liked it.
itens.porque: Maya's first line, word for word. At speed the three words run into one another — and it is still a complete instruction.

itens.t: Let me think.
itens.porque: Chris says it before he explains. Three seconds bought out loud, and the same phrase is on the next screen as one of yours.

itens.t: I will give you that.
itens.porque: At normal speed this sounds like one long word — I'll give you that. It means: you are right about this one thing.

itens.t: Why do you not like it?
itens.porque: Close, and not the same. Maya says Why do you say that? One attacks the opinion; the other asks for the reason. Only the second one gets an answer.

itens.t: I completely disagree.
itens.porque: Nobody says it. Chris disagrees for two minutes without ever using the word — which is part of why the conversation survives.

itens.t: It is too slow.
itens.porque: He says It is just slow. Too would be a complaint; just is a description, and he has already said the movie is not bad.

red20.rationale: The three real ones are the three that disappear at speed. The three false ones are what a careful reader expects to hear — which is exactly why they are hard.

opcoes: giving something to the other side

itens.t: Really? Why do you say that?
itens.porque: Maya's move, and the one that produces the longest turn in the conversation.

itens.t: Um, let me think.
itens.porque: It says nothing about the movie and keeps his turn. Without it there would be three seconds of silence and Maya would start talking again.

itens.t: The photography is beautiful. I will give you that.
itens.ok: giving something to the other side
itens.porque: He is losing nothing by saying it, and the rest of what he says becomes believable because of it.

itens.t: Why do you love it so much?
itens.porque: Same move as Maya's, from the other side. In a real conversation both people do this.

itens.t: That is a good question.
itens.porque: It compliments the question and answers nothing. Perfectly polite, and it is four seconds.

itens.t: It is not bad. It is just slow.
itens.ok: giving something to the other side
itens.porque: He agrees that it is not bad and keeps his own word, slow. Two ideas, one sentence, and nobody has to lose.

mv20.rationale: Two of each. Notice that only two of the six are about the movie at all — the other four are about keeping the conversation open.

abertura: The three moves, and what each one is for.

callout.texto:
You kept a conversation going with someone who disagreed with you, and you did it without going quiet once.

Go back to what Maya and Chris did: she asks him for the reason, he buys himself some time before he answers, he gives her the photography, and at the end he asks her the same question back. Nothing on that list is vocabulary about movies. All of it works on any subject, in any conversation, starting today.

speakmore.pt:
Grave um recado curto de voz, se quiser. É opcional: nada aqui é corrigido nem cobrado na próxima aula.

A situação: alguém disse alguma coisa de que você discorda completamente — sobre uma série, uma música ou uma decisão na escola. Discorde, dê o seu motivo, e termine perguntando alguma coisa a essa pessoa.

abertura: Write a six-message chat between two people who disagree, like the one in the pre-class.

callout.texto:
Nobody wins, and the conversation is still going at the sixth message.

Put all three moves in it: one person asks for the reason, one buys time, and one gives something to the other side.

writemore.pt:
Escreva uma conversa de chat de seis mensagens entre duas pessoas que discordam, como a do exercício 4.

A regra: ninguém ganha, e na sexta mensagem a conversa ainda está de pé. Ponha os três movimentos lá dentro — alguém pede o motivo, alguém ganha tempo, e alguém dá alguma coisa para o outro lado.

itens.texto: A list of ways to disagree, from the gentle to the very direct, with examples. Find the two you would actually use — the rest are for reading, not for saying.
Ways to give an opinion and, more useful, ways to ask for someone else's. Look for the ones that end with a question — those are the ones that keep a conversation going.
